messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] SEV2 — spike in 5xx rate for /v1/generate on prod. alert_id=alert-64321. Start=2026-03-15T02:17:14Z. Paging @eng-oncall.

Alex Chen: I got the page. Seeing 5xx rate jump from ~0.4% -> ~6% in last 5m across eu-west1 and us-central. Latency OK. No deploys in last 30m per deploy-bot.

Alex Chen: digging into logs now, adding quick query to the dashboard.

Jordan Reyes: looping in Priya (oncall next). Priya are you able to take lead if this persists?

Priya Patel: taking over. Alex, can you share the query you ran? also any customer-facing incidents flagged?

Alex Chen: query pasted below. short term: I'll enable prefix cache bypass logs to check KV hits.

```
# datadog log query
service:api-prod AND route:"/v1/generate" AND http.status_code:[500 TO 599] @timestamp >= now-10m
```

Alex Chen: right now errors concentrated on one worker pool (gpu-5). Stack traces look like transient OOM-ish but also 503 upstream from model-host in a subset of hosts.

Marta Lopez: thanks. Priya, if errors >=5% for 10m i'd escalate to sev1. For now treat as sev2. Two parallel actions: 1) mitigate customer impact, 2) reduce alert noise and avoid paging for known transient flaps.

Priya Patel: mitigation: enabling fallback routing to warm replica pool for affected requests. Command below to flip routing rule for 2m window:

```
# ops-console command (internal)
ops route set-fallback --service api-prod --route /v1/generate --target pool:warm-replicas --duration 2m --by=priority
```

Priya Patel: executing now.

Jordan Reyes: ack. Also I suggest we silence the per-host 5xx alert which is noisy and only page on cluster-wide rate. Can someone make that change?

Marta Lopez: agreed. Action: change alert-64321 definition -> only page when cluster 5xx rate > 4% for 5m, and keep host-level alerts as non-pager with 1m notify to #eng-sre. Add a duplicate low-severity alert to catch regressions.

Alex Chen: I can file the alert edit now in Datadog. Will annotate the change and link runbook.

Alex Chen: creating alert edit: alert-64321 -> threshold 4% over 5m, scope: service:api-prod, route:/v1/generate. Also adding a mute window for deploy windows.

Priya Patel: confirmed fallback routing took effect at 2026-03-15T02:22:10Z. Error rate dropping to ~1.2% now. Customers with active sessions may see degraded generations for a minute. No major customer reports so far.

incident-bot: [NOTE] incident annotated: incident-20260315-01 created.

Marta Lopez: good. Once stabilized, we need a quick postmortem and runbook update. Items to update:
- runbook: add decision tree for fallback routing and thresholds
- alerting: change pager thresholds + host-level dedupe and non-pager
- dashboards: new per-route error heatmap by region and by host pool
- ownership: assign alert and runbook to 'Priya Patel' and add SRE reviewer

Priya Patel: I'll take ownership of the runbook and the alert change. Will create a PR against internal runbooks page and add links to the incident. Runbook URL: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/api-errors (will add PR link after).

Alex Chen: created Datadog alert edit: https://app.datadog.com/monitors/64321 — note in description: "tuned 2026-03-15 after transient model-host flaps; owners: Priya Patel, SRE". Also added a timeframe to avoid paging during known infra maintenance windows.

Priya Patel: creating a follow-up task in the oncall board: "review alert-64321 tuning and add dashboard" — linking to ticket: https://redwood-internal/tasks/INC-5237

Jordan Reyes: please add a dashboard panel showing 95th latency and 5xx rate side-by-side with per-pool distribution. That'll help next time.

Alex Chen: added annotation to the dashboard at 2026-03-15T02:22:10Z: "incident-20260315-01: fallback routing enabled; errors down".

Marta Lopez: quick note for runbook content: include exact ops-console commands, Datadog monitor IDs, and decision thresholds. Example snippet to add to runbook: 

```
When cluster 5xx rate >= 4% for 5m: 
  - verify if concentrated on single pool/host -> if yes, enable fallback routing to warm-replicas for 2m
  - if error persists >10m escalate to SRE lead and page oncall-sv1
  - document mitigation in incident ticket and annotate dashboard
```

Priya Patel: will post runbook PR after this thread and ping for review. Assigning reviewer: Marta Lopez.

Jordan Reyes: one more: add a Prometheus-style aggregation in alerts to dedupe per-host spikes: `sum(rate(http_errors[5m])) by (cluster,route)` instead of per-host. That should reduce noise.

Alex Chen: noted. I'll update the monitor query accordingly and keep non-pager host alerts for operational visibility.

Priya Patel: incident now resolved for user impact at 2026-03-15T02:30:05Z. Root cause: transient model-host pool experiencing a cache eviction storm after a telemetry job overloaded disk I/O. We have a separate ticket to address root cause: https://redwood-internal/issues/ROOT-411.

Marta Lopez: sweet. Post-incident actions assigned:
- Priya: runbook PR + alert monitor change (due 2026-03-18)
- Alex: dashboard panel + monitor annotation (done)
- Jordan: create perf ticket for model-host eviction mitigation (ROOT-411 owner)

Priya Patel: filing runbook PR now. PR link: https://git.redwood/internal/runbooks/pulls/278 — includes markdown with commands, thresholds, and a short FAQ.

Alex Chen: leaving a short post in #customer-impact: "Minor transient errors briefly affected /v1/generate; mitigated; no broad customer impact." tagging support.

incident-bot: [CLOSE] incident-20260315-01 closed by Priya Patel at 2026-03-15T02:34:05Z.

Priya Patel: thanks all. We'll do a quick 15m sync on Friday to review the alert thresholds and the new dashboard.

Marta Lopez: thanks team. Closing thread, moving follow-ups to INC-5237. :thumbsup:
